props.title: Frost/Nixon
props.initialSlug: Epic duel between disgraced Nixon and TV host

sections.content: Frost/Nixon masterfully adapts Peter Morgan's stage play into a riveting political thriller about the historic 1977 television interviews between British journalist David Frost and disgraced former president Richard Nixon. Director Ron Howard transforms what could have been static talking heads into a psychological boxing match, with Frank Langella's towering performance as Nixon going toe-to-toe with Michael Sheen's ambitious Frost. The film joins classics like All the President's Men (1976) and The Post (2017) in dramatizing Watergate-era political journalism, but focuses uniquely on Nixon's post-resignation life and quest for redemption.

sections.content: The film excels in depicting the high-stakes nature of television journalism, joining other masterful explorations like Network (1976) and Broadcast News (1987). Howard builds incredible tension around the interview preparation, with both men's careers and reputations hanging in the balance. The supporting cast, including Kevin Bacon as Nixon's protective chief of staff and Sam Rockwell as Frost's research team leader, adds layers of strategic complexity to the central duel.

What elevates Frost/Nixon beyond a mere historical recreation is its examination of power, pride, and redemption. Like The Queen (2006) and Nixon (1995), the film humanizes its controversial subject while never excusing their actions. The famous "drunk dial" scene, where Nixon calls Frost late at night, reveals the deep insecurities driving both men's ambitions. SUBHEAD: The Art of the Political Interview

sections.content: The film's climactic interviews showcase the power of careful questioning and strategic patience, similar to the interrogation techniques shown in Spotlight (2015) and The Insider (1999). Howard brilliantly captures the subtle shifts in power dynamics, with close-ups revealing psychological warfare through micro-expressions and pregnant pauses.
